trigger: an rpm database (sqlite, ndb or bdb) whose headers each carry one large NUL-terminated string region (up to the 32 MiB header cap) that NAME, VERSION, RELEASE, ARCH, VENDOR and PACKAGER all point at; needs a crafted or tampered database or a crafted package installed by root
summary: RpmHeader::string() copies each string tag independently with no per-field cap, while the byte budget charges the header once; probe: 8,388,713-byte blob -> 50,331,648 retained bytes (x6.0), so up to ~6 GiB at the 1 GiB total budget inside the 20 s wall, ~12 GiB with the AppInfo/InvRecord copies; no MemoryMax on the packaged unit. Derived HIGH via the I5(a) raise (reproducible agent-process unavailability on the daily-sync path); the security reviewer's native MEDIUM and the unhappy-path reviewer's HIGH disagreed, the derived band governs the gate. Fix: cap each string tag (oversized) or charge retained string bytes to the budget.
classification_rationale: no bound on retained string bytes; pkgdb_budget.hpp header contract says no allocation from a length not first checked against the byte budget

severity_native: HIGH on the table, MEDIUM in practice
trigger: (a) an rpm database file left on a pacman/apk host with no rpm binary (found with zero rows ends detection, pacman/apk never run); (b) a dpkg status holding only non-installed stanzas on an rpm host (parser keeps them, packages not empty, rpm never read)
summary: read_host_packages treats a found rpm database (L615) and a non-empty parsed dpkg set (L600) as final even when they yield zero emitted rows; the old binary-order cascade needed the tool binary, so a database without its binary is newly reachable. list/query then print an empty result as complete (list_inventory is protected by the no_rows guard). Also reported by happy-path (HP-2) and docs-writer (D2) as the docs saying 'falls through' while the code does not. Borderline on likelihood; derived HIGH by I3 base with E5 no change. Fix: fall through to the next leg when rpm is found with zero rows and when dpkg yields zero installed rows; align banner/README/ADR wording.
classification_rationale: banner, README caveat 3 and ADR say an empty/no-installed-package status falls through; code falls through only on an empty parsed vector

classification_rationale: manual cleanup in new test code; the floor text does not exempt tests

trigger: daily sync lands during an rpm transaction on a BDB (RHEL 8) or ndb (SUSE) database: the reader takes no rpm lock (.rpm.lock) and its before/after stamp has coarse (jiffy) ctime granularity on kernels before 6.13, so a write in the same tick as the last pre-stamp write leaves the stamp equal
summary: MANDATORY INVESTIGATION (derived HIGH, speculative so a deferral of the decision, not a dismissal): resolve to verified, likely or refuted before the gate passes. Evidence needed: can the BDB/ndb data file be read mid-transaction and parse as a consistent-looking roster; does the old rpm -qa path take a shared lock that this reader skips. Candidate fix if confirmed: F_GETLK probe on .rpm.lock mapped to the existing locked cause, and a racy-stamp re-check; lane run on alma8 (reinstall loop diffed against rpm -qa). Merges unhappy-path UP-3 and UP-4; sqlite is unaffected (snapshot isolation).
classification_rationale: no lock or racy-stamp handling for in-place-written rpm formats

trigger: dpkg interrupted mid-unpack leaves /var/lib/dpkg/updates/*; this reader does not read it
summary: MANDATORY INVESTIGATION (derived HIGH, speculative): does dpkg-query -W merge the updates journal into what it prints; if it does, the reader lags the old path on an interrupted host. Resolve by dpkg source or one lane check (kill -9 dpkg mid-unpack, diff). If dpkg-query does not merge it, record refuted with the evidence.
classification_rationale: journal not read

trigger: agent stop or reconnect while a package-database read is slow or wedged; the old subprocess leg polled subprocess_cancel_requested (set at stop), the in-process read polls only g_pkgdb_stop, raised in shutdown() after the sync thread joined
summary: stop lambda should also test yuzu::agent::subprocess_cancel_requested() (already available via the included subprocess_runner.hpp) so a slow-but-progressing read ends promptly; a wedged pread stays bounded by the 20 s wall. Folds: no new surface.
classification_rationale: comment claims the stop flag ends the worker; the flag is raised too late to cover agent stop

trigger: an rpm database that is EMPTY in usr/lib/sysimage/rpm and var/lib/rpm a symlink to a DIFFERENT directory that holds the populated database (a layout the reader never follows); the plugin then runs its pacman leg, finds nothing, and `list`/`query` print an empty, non-degraded result
summary: The up-10 fix suppresses rpmdb:symlink_refused whenever ANY database was read (`if (symlinked_db && !db_read)`), but its stated reason (code comment :788-790, banner) is only the Fedora/RHEL/SUSE layout where var/lib/rpm links to the directory just read. For a link to some other directory the refusal is suppressed too, so a populated database behind a never-followed link reads as "ecosystem none, no failure". Probe on braga (scratch root, real fedora41 fixture, Apple clang): empty sysimage db + var/lib/rpm -> populated dir elsewhere gives eco=none rpm=0 failure=''; the same link with nothing else read gives rpmdb:symlink_refused; the Fedora layout (link to the same dir) reads 4 rows. Derived HIGH (I3, E5, verified) with the trigger a doubly unusual admin layout; which directory is authoritative depends on the host's rpm dbpath, so the wrong outcome is established only where the link target is the dbpath. Borderline, as up-10 was: the Architect may adjudicate the band with an independent adjudicated_by. Fix: suppress the refusal only when the skipped link resolves to a directory already read (compare st_dev/st_ino of the link target with the opened directory descriptor), else keep symlink_refused; add the layout to the tests (empty db + link elsewhere => symlink_refused; empty db + link to itself => none).
classification_rationale: the code comment says the suppression is for a link to the directory just read; the code suppresses for every link once a database was read

Fold: one sentence in each of the three, README fences and plugin-docs JSON regenerated with the repo generator, never hand-edited.
classification_rationale: required doc items 2 (user-manual section) and 3 (changelog fragment) of the shared preamble list

severity_native: NICE (derived MEDIUM; native and derived disagree)
trigger: an ndb or Berkeley DB host where an administrator made .rpm.lock unreadable to the agent account (mode 0600 or 0640 root-only); the open gives EACCES, mapped to rpm_ndb:unreadable / rpm_bdb:unreadable on every read; the old rpm -qa never opened that file
summary: rpm_transaction_refusal maps any open error other than ENOENT to its own cause, so an unreadable lock file refuses the read (fail closed, named token, stored rows kept). Mapping verified by probe (mode 000, non-root). Reachability unresolved: rpm is believed to create the file 0644, not verified, and the lane step already owes a check that the unprivileged account can open it. Not a code change (failing closed is right); document the token and the mode assumption. Fold with the docs batch and prove on the lane.
classification_rationale: README caveat for the lock-file read is missing the unreadable-lock-file case (shared preamble required doc item 2)

classification_rationale: prose precision only; the domain agent for (a) is architect, who confirmed the behaviour is the ruled one

summary: Fixed in 085292788c: PkgDbBudget::kept_left and charge_kept (agents/shared/pkgdb_budget.hpp:111), RpmHeader::text returning string_view and rpm_package_from_header(h, budget) charging every kept string before its copy (agents/shared/rpmdb_parsers.hpp:152, 245-253), Limits::rpm_max_kept_bytes = 8 MiB set at read_rpm_dir (installed_apps_pkgdb_read.hpp:120, 697). Re-verified in round 2 by two independent reviewers: six aliased tags pass only if 6L <= 8 MiB; a 32 MiB string fails on the first charge; the aliased-string test goes red if charge_kept is removed.

Fixed in 085292788c: dpkg is the answer only when a stanza is `installed` (installed_apps_pkgdb_read.hpp:760), an empty rpm database continues to the next candidate (:775-786), and symlink_refused needs `symlinked_db && !db_read` (:791); tests cover all five sections of the r1 ruling. A residual of the same fix (a link to a different directory after an empty database) is recorded as r2-up-10b-empty-db-with-link-to-other-dir.

Fixed in 085292788c: tests/unit/test_rpmdb_parsers.cpp blobs_of_sqlite owns the connection (before the REQUIRE on the open result) and the statement (declared after it, finalized first) with std::unique_ptr; no manual cleanup remains in new test code (round 2 grep of the delta).

Fixed in 085292788c, refined in 9ee0a151bd: rpm_transaction_refusal (installed_apps_pkgdb_read.hpp:612-629, called at :690 for ndb and Berkeley DB only, after the first stamp and before the first read) opens .rpm.lock through the database directory descriptor (leaf not followed, O_NONBLOCK) and asks fcntl(F_GETLK) for a whole-file write lock; locked refuses the read; ENOENT is not locked; any other open error or a failed query is its own cause. It never takes a lock. Resolved to likely from the rpm source in the round 1 ruling (every writer holds the transaction lock, no reader does). Closed by construction; the held-lock cases run on Linux only and the lane must show them executed.

Fixed in 085292788c: dpkg_updates_failure (installed_apps_pkgdb_read.hpp:355-388, called from read_dpkg at :426) lists var/lib/dpkg/updates by name through walk_dir_capped, a digits-only name is dpkg_updates:locked with the status packages discarded, an absent directory is no journal, a link, non-directory or failed listing is a named failure. Premise verified in round 2 from dpkg source (lib/dpkg/dbmodify.c: modstatdb_open calls cleanupdates for every mode but lock-only, and cleanupdates parses every digits-named file of the updates directory; write-back and unlink only at write access), so dpkg-query -W printed the merged view.

Fixed in 085292788c: the readers' expired predicate is g_pkgdb_stop || yuzu::agent::subprocess_cancel_requested() (installed_apps_plugin.cpp:419-424); the latch is set only at agent stop and never cleared in production; include and link verified in round 2; lexical gate mutations pin it.

Fixed in 085292788c (changelog fragment, docs/user-manual/inventory.md, README, ADR-0016); round 2 residuals are recorded as r2-d1-status-vocabulary-undocumented, r2-cx1-rpm-lock-file-eacces and r2-docs-wording-batch.
Fixed in 085292788c: tests/test_installed_apps_pkgdb_wiring_lexical.py pins the failure-return shape and the stop predicate (mutations 15-17); the script passes (rc 0, 2 tests).

Fixed in 085292788c and 9ee0a151bd: tests/unit/test_installed_apps_pkgdb.cpp covers the ctime stamp, the ndb/bdb shell row cap, short read and EINTR in fd_source, and the progress handler; new cases cover each r1 blocking fix.
Fixed in 085292788c; round 2 wording residuals are folded into r2-docs-wording-batch.

Refuted in round 2 against dpkg source: lib/dpkg/dbmodify.c update_file_filter selects digits-only names and, when a name is longer than DPKG_DB_IMPORTANT_MAXLEN, calls ohshit ("updates directory contains file ... whose name is too long"), so dpkg and dpkg-query themselves fail on such a name; the old path therefore degraded too, and dpkg_updates:locked (a named degraded answer, rows kept) is the same class of outcome, not a defect.
refuted_by: curl of https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guillemj/dpkg/main/lib/dpkg/dbmodify.c, lines 63-85 (update_file_filter: digits-only, ohshit when l > DPKG_DB_IMPORTANT_MAXLEN) and 380 (cleanupdates called for every mode but lock-only)
refuted_by_reporter: governance runner, round 2 (a governance agent; not the change author)
